Date : 21/04/2023  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
Heard learned advocates for the parties.
Perused the record.

The appellants herein are original claimants before the C/FA/1827/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of Anand in Motor Accident Claims Petition No.3937 of 2006 (Old No.2805 of 1999), being mother, widow and three children of the deceased.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal of Anand
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Petition No.3937 of 2006
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: They have preferred such petition claiming compensation for the accidental death of one Bakabhai.

It is undisputed fact that on 20.07.1999 deceased was coming from Vataman to Tarapur driving Chakado bearing No. GJ 1 U 7301 and when he reached near Kasbara Patiya, the driver of the truck No. GJ 3 U 6006 came in wrong side in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed and dashed with the chakado, resulting into fatal injuries to the victim who died on the spot.
2.
The only issue in this appeal is with regard to the quantum of compensation that may be awarded to the claimants.

The tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.3,99,400/-, considering the Rs.2600/-
as prospective income, yearly which comes to Rs.31,200/- and thereafter deducting 1/4th i.e.
Rs.7800/- as his personal expenses and thereby considering yearly dependency loss as Rs.23,400/-.
Considering the age of the victim as 35 years, tribunal has applied 16 as a suitable multiplier and thereby awarded Rs.3,74,400/- under the head of dependency.
To such amount the tribunal has added Rs.5000/- for funeral expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards consortium and Rs.10,000/- towards expectations of life.
Thereby, the tribunal has awarded Rs.3,99,400/- as compensation.
3. Learned advocate for the appellants - claimants has submitted that the tribunal has failed to consider the proper income of the deceased - victim.

He has relied upon a C/FA/1827/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Laxmi Devi vs.
Mohammad Tabar reported in 2008 ACJ 1488 , wherein it is held that Rs.3000/- should be considered as notional income and submitted that such ratio is applicable to the present case and that the tribunal ought to have considered Rs.3000/- as monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text:
Laxmi Devi vs.
Mohammad Tabar reported in 2008 ACJ 1488
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3.1 Learned advocate for the appellants - claimants also relied upon another decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Rajesh vs. Rajbirsingh reported in 2013 ACJ 1403 , wherein in para 11 it is held that in case of self employed person or a person with fixed wages below the age of 40 years,
there must be an addition of 50% to the actual income of the deceased while computing future prospects.

entities.text: Rajesh vs. Rajbirsingh reported in 2013 ACJ 1403
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has submitted that in present case also the deceased - victim was aged about 35 hears and therefore, the same ratio is applicable to the present case also.

He has also relied upon the same decision in case of Rajesh (supra), wherein in para 21 it is held that in absence of evidence to the contrary for higher expenses, to award at least an amount of Rs.25,000/- under the head of funeral expenses.
Thereby, he has requested to allow the present appeal by enhancing the awarded amount suitably.
4. Learned advocate for the respondent No.3 - insurance company has supported the impugned award and submitted that this Court may not interfere with the impugned award.

entities.text: Makwana Rupben Chhaganbhai vs Balvantsinh Mansinh Rayjada
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After hearing the learned advocates appearing for the parties and after perusing the record, it is clear that the tribunal has failed to consider proper income of the deceased C/FA/1827/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 victim, so also the prospective earning capacity and also not considered just and reasonable compensation under the heads of loss of estate, loss of consortium etc.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to modify the award by enhancing the amount of compensation as under;
5.1 It is undisputed fact that claimants have not claimed any exhaustive amount.
It is submitted that deceased was driving chakado rickshaw and earning Rs.3000/- per month and also supervising agricultural work and earning Rs.15000/- per annum.
Thereby, deceased was earning Rs.4250/- per month.

However, if we consider that by driving chakado rickshaw, there would not be any fix income and in agricultural work also there would not be any fix income, then also Rs.2600/- as calculated by the tribunal is certainly on lower side.
As such, if we consider Rs.3000/- as his monthly income and to such amount, if we add Rs.1200/- as his prospective income, then total would be Rs.4200/-.

From such amount, if we deduct again Rs.1050/- taking 1/4th towards personal expenses, Rs.3150/- would be monthly dependency of the claimants and Rs.37,800/-
would be yearly dependency and after applying 16 as multiplier as done by the tribunal, the claimants are entitled to Rs.6,04,800/- towards loss of dependency.

5.2 Moreover, considering the judgment of full bench of the Honourable Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680 claimants are entitled to total Rs.70,000/- in aggregate in different conventional heads.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi reported in 2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case of Sarla Verma &
Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in Air 2009 SC 3104, C/FA/1827/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 the Honourable Supreme Court has held that the amount of personal expenses which the deceased would have spend on himself has he been alive from his monthly income should be determined on the basis of number of dependents.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma &
Ors. vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in Air 2009 SC 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram @ Chugru Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the Honourable Supreme Court has held as under;
"The Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation aimed at providing relief to the victims or their families, in cases of genuine claims.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd vs. Nanu Ram @ Chugru Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental Consortium is awarded to children who lose their parents in motor vehicle accidents under the Act.
The amount of compensation to be awarded as consortium will be governed by the principles of awarding compensation under 'Loss of Consortium' as laid down in Pranay Sethi (supra)."
5.3 Therefore, in view of settled legal position as above, claimants are entitled to Rs.1,20,000/- as consortium, Rs.15000/- as loss of estate and Rs.15000/- as funeral expenses.
Thereby, claimants are entitled to total Rs.7,54,800/-.

Whereas the tribunal has awarded Rs.3,99,400/- and, therefore,
claimants are entitled to enhanced amount of Rs.3,55,400/- with the interest at the rate of 7.5%
from the date of original petition.

The insurance company shall deposit the enhanced C/FA/1827/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 21/04/2023 amount with interest within 6 weeks from the Makwana Rupben Chhaganbhai vs Balvantsinh Mansinh Rayjada on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49476121/
3 date of this order before the tribunal.
6.

entities.text: Makwana Rupben Chhaganbhai vs Balvantsinh Mansinh Rayjada
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of above, appeal is allowed as above and disposed of accordingly.
Record and Proceedings be sent back to the concerned tribunal forthwith.
